title: [Enhancement] Inventory Database for Insulin, Test-Strips and Sensors
body:
Hi,

it would be nice if xdrip+ have a inventory database where I can set my amount of Insulin Pens (long-lasting like Lantus or Toujeo and rapid like FIASP or Novorapid), amount of (Dexcom or Abbott) Sensors and Test-Strip for calibration. When I input a Insulin-treatment it reduces the amount of Insulin Units in the pen and predict how long the actual pen last (based on the consumption maybe on the last 3, 7 or 14 days), how long all of my pens lasts. When I start a new sensors it reduces the amount of sensors and say 'In x weeks there are no more sensors if every sensors lasts the full 14 days', when I input a new calibration it reduces the amount of test-strips by at least one, or manually more, if I waste one with too little blood or something else went wrong during the measurement.

That would be during the usage no more hassle (beside the start-amount of everything) but gives me an relative precise overview of my stuff and when I have to order something new or obtain a new prescription.

comments.body: that would actually be suprisingly handy!

Test strips Rx's are based on average strip usage per day; your doctor writes an Rx for strips based on your needs and that in turn becomes the quantity you get from your pharmacy.  Once your usage is determined, you'll get x number of strips per month or every 3 months, etc.  Your meter can be downloaded, and in the report it will state your average usage per day which is what your doc should be going by when creating Rx's for your strips.   Therefore I see no need for that functionality in xDrip (to reduce quantity-on-hand, for strips--it's not necessary).

> Test strips Rx's are based on average strip usage per day; your doctor writes an Rx for strips based on your needs and that in turn becomes the quantity you get from your pharmacy. Once your usage is determined, you'll get x number of strips per month or every 3 months, etc. Your meter can be downloaded, and in the report it will state your average usage per day which is what your doc should be going by when creating Rx's for your strips. Therefore I see no need for that functionality in xDrip (to reduce quantity-on-hand, for strips--it's not necessary).

i would find it useful personally as i don't go through a set amount of insulin / strips every month it varies greatly. i contact my pharmacy to place orders when needed, so having a inventory of strips / sensors / insulin built into xdrip i would find helpful and avoid times that i have used the last of my strips without knowing it.

Interesting.  I can see how many boxes of strips I have left in inventory by looking at my "stash" area.  No need to refer to a database.  Same with insulin.  All non-working bottles are kept in the fridge in a butter drawer devoted to the task.  Physical items are easy to keep track of when they aren't scattered about, so I'm not digging your idea that you need to input quantity data into ANY sort of database.  I'm just not following your methodology for knowing what you have on hand.  To me, it seems like a solution in search of a problem.  :)

Okay, let me put in another aspect. I travel a lot and only goes to my Doc 4 times a year. I want to know if I last with my equipment till the next 3-4 month or if I 'survive' the next long trip or if I need to refill my 'stash' area. And I normally have tree areas were I store my stuff, the refrigerator, the cupboard and my daily pouch. At the moment I don't see easily how much insulin I 'consume' over a given period (last 4 weeks for instance) nor can I easy can estimate when I run out of something. Yes, it is not that complicated to calculate that, but xDrip currenly have all data, the amount of consumed insulin, the test strips, when you start a new sensors, only if I don't use every time a new needles I have to give it this information on top. I would code this information by myself, but I currently don't have a good idea where to start.

Did you have experience with Java/Android studio? Then I think a good.place could be the status area, or maybe an own menuentry in the three dots menu. Try it, xdrip lives from all devs, and you could be part of it ;)
I'm closing this due to inactivity.  We can always reopen it if there is a need and if there are developers who are interested.
